title: Immersion Library
description: Choose from several trusted Hawaiian-language collections and listen without turning immersion into a test.

sourceReview.notes: The immersion library now favors reliable source collections and video/podcast series over embedding individual legacy MP3 files. Each collection is presented for exposure, not mastery.

activities.support: A 13-episode Hawaiian language learning series from ʻŌiwi TV. Episodes combine hearing, participation, language instruction, and cultural context.
listeningNotes: Start with Episode 1 if you want structured beginner material.
Replay episodes freely; the series is designed so learners can set their own pace.
Listen for familiar words and patterns without trying to translate everything.

activities.support: A free Kamehameha Schools Hawaiian-language video series hosted by ʻEkela Kanīʻaupiʻo Crozier, with 24 lessons available online.
listeningNotes: Use the video format for both listening and visual context.
You can follow the lessons in order or revisit a lesson that interests you.
Workbooks/transcripts are available for some lessons if you want support after listening.

activities.support: A conversational podcast about learning and using Hawaiian at home. Good for longer-form listening and hearing how learners discuss language use in everyday life.
listeningNotes: Treat this as conversational immersion rather than a formal lesson.
Notice Hawaiian words and phrases as they appear naturally in discussion.
Longer episodes are useful for background listening as well as focused sessions.

activities.instruction: Use this archive when the audio works well in your browser.
activities.support: The official UH Hilo HAW 101 podcast archive by Kumu Kainani Kahaunaele. Keep it as an optional resource rather than the main immersion experience because the older MP3 delivery can be inconsistent.
activities.audioSourceName: Ka Haka ʻUla O Keʻelikōlani — UH Hilo
listeningNotes: Use this collection when playback behaves normally on your device.
If a file cuts off or seeking fails, switch to one of the video/podcast collections above.
The archive remains valuable as an official HAW 101 resource, but it is no longer the app's primary immersion source.
